children: BEER JUG: A VERY GERMAN INFLATION INDICATOR

Germany is known for its beer, and by extension for Munich's Oktoberfest - the long-running folk festival turned massive tourism event where beer is drank in a 'Maß' - the measure for a litre jug of the drink.
The price of a Maß is always a hot topic of conversation, but could it also have a bigger purpose?

"The longevity of the Oktoberfest has an advantage for economists: the price of a Maß of beer provides a wonderfully simple alternative inflation gauge," Andreas Rees, chief German economist at UniCredit, suggested.

This year, a Maß will set you back an average of 15.61 euro, which is a 2.4% increase from last year - and while that may sound substantial, it's actually the smallest rise in two decades according to Rees.
It also notably falls short of euro zone inflation expectations for the year - although historically, Maß price growth has far outpaced that of consumer prices more broadly, Rees said.
"Beer prices at the Oktoberfest depend on a peculiar cocktail of harvests, energy prices, wages, tent costs, security and the willingness of millions of visitors to spend generously," he explained.

Some of those factors are of course clearly linked to classic inflation measures - but the more beer- and event- specific ones do seem to complicate any potential high level inflation forecasting matters, so you might want to exercise some caution before rushing to base any decisions on Maß-flation.
"Forecasting consumer-price inflation is difficult enough; forecasting inflation with a foam head may be even harder," Rees said.
